keyFindings.description: Blocking, and it lives inside this round's own fix: a refused setting reaches the agent only when the run installs cleanly. `write_report` puts `setting_note` at the head of `detail` and up to 1000 bytes of install log follow it, while the notice quotes `detail.slice(-400)` (packages/pi-legion/src/setup-report.ts:81-82), so for every reason that carries a log the sentence is cut off. Measured through the real `setupReportNotice`: a 1,079-character detail whose head is `LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_HOLD=60s is not a whole number of seconds …` yields a notice containing neither that variable nor that phrase. The script's own header (:30-32) and the implementer's round-4 reply both say a failing run carries the sentence — true of the JSON, false of the only thing the agent reads. Remedy: a field of its own rendered for both kinds, or keep the head as well as the tail.

`reason=lock-timeout` still labels the one path that did hold the lock and install — the retry that lost the `flock` race on its second attempt. The marker decision and the detail are now right (they turn on `first_status`), but `ranInstall` excludes `lock-timeout`, so that run's genuine install log is introduced as `It reported:`, and setup-report.ts:88-90 describes only the run that never installed. Nothing the agent is told is untrue. The `case`'s `"$LOCK_BUSY") reason=lock-timeout` arm is also read only where it is false, since the branch below writes the literal itself: hoisting that branch above the `case` and dropping the arm removes the duplicate literal and the mislabel together.

An unbalanced-quote line now yields no comment, so no marker can be read from it, yet the message printed for it still ends by offering `check-check-commands: allow <reason>`. Reproduced: a fixture line carrying that exact marker after an unbalanced quote is reported, with the message offering the marker the author already wrote. Say that the quoting could not be read instead.

This pull request's own entry still says the report is one "which a successful install deletes" and names only `install-failed`, after this round added `setting-ignored`, which a successful install writes instead of deleting. Same class as the defects the round fixed, in the published record of the package.

Outside this round's fixes, and recorded rather than requested: an unclosed fence under a label the gate does not judge (```text, ```json, an unknown language) still leaves every later line of the file unjudged until a bare fence, with nothing printed. Identical at 5bee2e95 and at this head, so it predates the session-fence fix that closed the same class on the judged path. No judged guide in the tree holds an unclosed fence.

verified: Round 3's three findings re-checked by running them: a guide whose unclosed ```console block carries a prompt no longer un-judges the later ```sh block (reported here, silent at 5bee2e95); `echo "a # b && bunx biome check .` and its single-quote twin are reported, a marker quoted after an unbalanced quote exempts nothing, and a genuine trailing marker still exempts; `use_seconds` refuses 08, 00, 0, 060, -5, 1.5, 9223372036854775808 and a twenty-digit value with a note and the default, takes 90 and 9223372036854775807, and exits 0 in every case, driven on the image's dash. A well-formed prompted session block still has only its prompted lines judged. All 21 threads carry my answer.
CI at code head a8bc03bc: 24 check runs, none unsuccessful, `dispatch` completed success; the required lint, typecheck, test and pr-title green; compare a8bc03bc...b9bc9463 is .legion/ only.
